transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Because water has reached the plug area, there is an electrical hazard that only a professional can safely resolve. Regarding the leak itself: water pooling under a Beko washing machine usually comes from one of three places:
1. The drain pump or its filter housing (often leaks when draining).
2. An internal hose connection that has come loose or split.
3. A worn door seal or, less commonly but seriously, failed drum bearings (which would look like dark, oily water and make a grinding noise). Since the machine is still running, please stop it now via the controls if you can do so safely without touching wet parts, then switch off at the wall. To start narrowing this down: does the water look like clean tap water, or dirty/soapy wash water? And do you hear any loud grinding or rumbling noises from the drum?

It looks like clean water I think, not soapy. No grinding, just normal washing sounds. I'm standing in socks on the wet floor right now, should I get out of it? The consumer unit is in the hall, dry there

Yes, please get out of the water immediately. Standing in it is dangerous because electricity can travel through the water to you. Because the water has reached the plug area and the machine is still running, this is a serious electrical hazard. You must switch off the power at your consumer unit (fuse box) right now. 1. Stop the machine if you can do so safely from the controls without touching wet parts, otherwise leave it until an engineer attends.
2. Do not attempt to move the machine or check behind it yourself; water and electricity are a dangerous mix that requires a qualified professional to resolve safely. The leak is likely coming from the inlet valve (supplying clean tap water) or an internal hose connection, but because the water has reached the electrical socket, this is beyond owner-safe repair. Please call a qualified appliance engineer or electrician to inspect and fix both the leak and the safety hazard.

candidates: Leak from internal hose, pump, or seal (high)
